assign.outcome:
**Ready to merge: branch worktree/truth-score-endings, commits 33a8f1aef, df539f35e, bf268f208.**

- [x] A session with nothing to score reads null, shown as needs review: `completion.test.mjs`, 37 checks pass.
- [x] A parent's mean skips nulls, `tally().unscored` counts them, callers show it through `Task.show`.
- [x] Closing under 100% files one waiting task listing the open items, once, even on replay: `Servex/OpenItems.test.mjs`, 23 checks pass (one open plus one done gives exactly one; 100% gives none).
- [x] `list_waiting` lists those tasks.
- [ ] Screenshots: shot at 400 and 1200 in `shots/`, layout unchanged; the new Score text appears only after a Servex restart.

Left: a Servex restart is needed (changes under `Servex/` and `Server/`). No merge or review run by me.

findings.text: Servex `close_task` files no waiting task. `Servex/TaskLoop.js:10` only imports OpenItems: `TaskLoop.write_line` (worktree `Servex/TaskLoop.js:526`) never calls `OpenItems.after_write`. So the `complete` and `closed_by` lines that `close_task` writes (`TaskLoop.js:514-516`) and Dropped's lines (`TaskLoop.js:103`) skip the rule. The requirement names `close_task` as a chokepoint. `Servex/readme.md`, `core/Task/readme.md`, `doc/completion.md` and the header of `Servex/OpenItems.js` all say this hook is in place.

`OpenItems.test.mjs` never tests the `close_task` path. That is why finding 1 passed with 23 green checks. Add a case: run `TaskLoop.close_task` on a record that has one open task and one done task, and expect exactly one `open-items`.

Some closing paths still write without passing through the rule, yet the `Servex/OpenItems.js:72-73` comment says every path does. `Server/PromptRecords.mjs:127` and `Server/CloseoutWalk.mjs:138` (`--apply` writes `stop` lines) call `fs.appendFileSync` directly. `RecordWriter.append_once` (append.mjs and StaleClose when Servex is down) also appends raw. Either route these writes through the rule, or list them in the comment and the docs as known gaps.

The session page's new Score stat was never seen working. `shots/session-1200-after-worktree.png` only shows "This is a worktree preview, which is not allowed to ask Servex for numbers" on the Report tab: no stats bar and no "needs review". The handover admits this in its last log line. Shoot a no-task session on the main site after merge and restart.

The shot set is short. There is no `ai-1200-before-main.png` and no `session-400-before-main.png`, so two of the asked before/after pairs at 400 and 1200 are missing. The `ai-400` pair shows no layout change.

There may be a cost on every close. `OpenItems.after_write` runs inside the synchronous `write_line` in Servex. For every stop or complete line, it replays the whole record twice, plus up to two more replays in `reach()` for each filing, and child records are read from disk synchronously. `session-e00f55c9/session.jsonl` is 3.7 MB, so one close there could block Servex for a noticeable time. Worth measuring once.

Two remaining callers show a null score as "0%" (no throw): `public/framework/ai/sessions/doc/variants/SegBar.js:13` and `Server/PromptTrace.mjs:49` both do `Math.round(x.completion * 100)`. Route them through `Task.show` if they ever get a session.

Part of `core/Task/readme.md` is now stale. The old `completion` bullet right after the new text (diff line 605) still says "or 1 when complete", which is now wrong for a session. The new "No silent endings" bullet also ends with the formula link and the "Test: completion.test.mjs. The older description follows." text that belongs to the bullet above it.

The core design follows the brief. `Task.mean`/`Task.show`, the null result only when `is_session`, `tally().unscored`, the deterministic `open-items` id, and leaving closeout tasks out of `score_parts`/`reopened`/`complete()` all match it, and every decision has a log line. `completion.test.mjs` (37), `OpenItems.test.mjs` (23) and `session-query.test.mjs` all pass in the worktree. A fresh agent could pick this up from `plan.md`, `session.jsonl` and this review.
